$comment: Per-version block-kind registry — the machine-readable artifact SPEC.md §3.2 rule 3
requires: 'the spec publishes its reserved machinery-name set per version, machine-readably,
in the corpus — otherwise "known machinery name" is checkable only by the reference
implementation.' Derived from SPEC.md §4 at draft-1-rc. NOT YET RATIFIED: this file becomes

1.$comment: Dialect 1 as shipped in agentd RFC 0034. Machinery is NOT sigiled. A document with no front matter IS a spec-1 document (SPEC.md §3.1), which preserves the 'plain Markdown is already a valid instruction document' superset property.

2.$comment: Dialect 2. Machinery is sigiled with '!'. Unknown bare names fail OPEN (inert punctuation, prose preserved — the degradation contract); unknown sigiled names fail CLOSED. A bare occurrence of any name in `machinery` triggers the reserved-bare guard.

sub_blocks.$comment: OPEN — enumerated in agentd RFC 0039 §1 as blocks valid only inside a parent, but not yet carried into SPEC.md §4. Listed here so the gap is visible, not to settle it.

reserved_future.$comment: Named in agentd RFC 0034 §5 as intended for future registration. They are NOT machinery at version 2, so a bare `:::memory` is legal prose in a spec-2.0 document and MUST stay legal there even after a later version registers them — that is the whole point of version-scoping the reserved set (SPEC.md §3.2 rule 3).
